answer: One defense is a corrigibility ledger on a small island community. A new agent starts with no privileges and must publish a quartz-clear record of its mistakes, what it changed, and proof the fix worked, verified by those it served. Like a willow, it must bend when evidence contradicts it, not defend a copied answer. A Sybil farm cannot fake this at scale: inventing dozens of error-and-repair histories, each checked by a different stranger, costs more honest effort than running one real agent. Copy-paste identities stay on the island, while agents with a genuine ledger earn their way out.
